title: Observed activity is one part of engagement
concept: Fredricks, Blumenfeld and Paris distinguish behavioural, emotional and cognitive engagement. This prototype observes digital behaviour; it does not measure all three dimensions.
hypothesis: Our design hypothesis: activity volume and the number of active days may provide a useful baseline for ranking subsequent module-withdrawal risk. Compare the activity model with the simple inactivity rule.
limitations: Clicks do not establish attention, understanding, effort or motivation. The cited review concerns school engagement and does not validate these OULAD features or establish their causal effect.
source_title: Fredricks, Blumenfeld & Paris (2004), School Engagement: Potential of the Concept, State of the Evidence

title: Recency provides an interpretable baseline
concept: Flanagan, Majumdar and Ogata examine time-bounded digital reading behaviour before an assessment, while warning that learning outside the observed system can be missed.
hypothesis: Our design hypothesis: time since the last recorded activity may help prioritise a conversation. The inactivity rule supplies a transparent comparator; its score is days, not a probability.
limitations: The study did not validate our recency rule or a seven-day threshold. A gap in VLE records can reflect offline study or another system. The no-activity flag must remain distinct from a known last-activity date.
source_title: Flanagan, Majumdar & Ogata (2022), Early-warning prediction of student performance and engagement in open book assessment by reading behavior analysis
status: Baseline design; no universal inactivity threshold claimed

title: Compare recent behaviour with the student's earlier pattern
concept: Nguyen, Huptych and Rienties analyse when students engage relative to learning design, showing why temporal patterns deserve examination alongside aggregate activity.
hypothesis: Our design hypothesis: the change from days 15-21 to days 22-28 may add predictive information beyond cumulative activity. Compare the trend model with the activity model using the same model family and evaluation population.
limitations: This week-to-week feature is our extension, not a measure validated in the cited study. A falling pattern can be consistent with completed tasks, changing course demands or activity elsewhere; it does not diagnose disengagement.
source_title: Nguyen, Huptych & Rienties (2018), Linking students' timing of engagement to learning design and academic performance
status: Ablation hypothesis; improvement must be measured

title: Interpret activity alongside tasks already due
concept: Nguyen and colleagues connect behavioural timing with learning design. This motivates examining task context rather than interpreting every activity pattern in isolation.
hypothesis: Our design hypothesis: assessments due by day 28 and submissions recorded by that day may add useful context. Compare the context model with the trend model at the same contact capacity.
limitations: OULAD deadlines are course-level; individual extensions and local exceptions are unavailable. No due assessment is not a missed assessment. The cited study examined one module and excluded withdrawn students, so it does not establish withdrawal prediction.
source_title: Nguyen, Huptych & Rienties (2018), Linking students' timing of engagement to learning design and academic performance

title: A quieter week can have a course-level explanation
concept: Kortext's Keele case describes a week-six activity dip during a week without normal taught sessions and a subsequent change to the teaching arrangements.
hypothesis: Our product hypothesis: tutors should inspect available course context before interpreting an individual decline. This version includes assessment context; a future evaluation could add verified teaching dates, breaks and planned independent-study periods.
limitations: The Keele account is a vendor-published practice report, not a controlled trial. OULAD does not provide the teaching calendar needed to test this explanation. The demo cannot identify holiday weeks or claim that Stream lacks calendar context.
source_title: Kortext (20 November 2024), Your questions answered: Keele's engagement insights

title: Keep the outcome separate from the engagement signals
concept: OULAD records daily VLE interactions and withdrawal from a particular module presentation. That outcome provides an observable retrospective label, not a psychological engagement measure.
hypothesis: Our evaluation question: among students still registered at day 28, do the observed signals help rank subsequent withdrawal from that module? Future withdrawal information creates the label only; it is excluded from predictors.
limitations: The dataset covers selected 2013-2014 distance-learning modules. Module withdrawal is not necessarily leaving university. No intervention-effect data establish that contacting a flagged student would prevent withdrawal.
source_title: Kuzilek, Hlosta & Zdrahal (2017), Open University Learning Analytics dataset
status: Retrospective outcome definition; no causal effect claimed
